The Literature of Sports in Ancient Greece. This class introduces ancient Greek sporting culture through the available textual evidence, including epigraphy, epinician poetry, and narrative prose. Intersecting social issues such as physical and mental health, personal identity, and civic identity will be discussed. Previous interest in sports is not required.

This seminar explores the dramatic oeuvre of Euripides through close readings of Trojan Women, the satyr play Cyclops, and selected fragmentary plays. Examining these texts, the course investigates how Euripides interrogates central themes of politics, gender, and trauma in classical Athens. Moving beyond the surviving tragic canon, the seminar demonstrates how satyr drama and fragmentary works expand our understanding of the much broader Euripidean corpus known in antiquity. This wider perspective engages questions of genre and performance while highlighting the diverse civic, religious, and cultural contexts of Athenian drama.
